 How and Where to Watch: Libya vs Tunisia LIVE on beIN SPORTS
 Libya hosts Tunisia after a 2-0 win in Sfax in the 2027 AFCON Qualifiers. The Mediterranean Knights aim to build on that result, while the Eagles of Carthage desperately seek their first victory.
 Watch Libya vs Tunisia LIVE on beIN SPORTS 
 Libya vs Tunisia: How and Where to Watch LIVE
 Matchday 4 of the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations Qualifiers brings another important North African showdown on Tuesday, November 17, as Libya welcomes Tunisia just four days after securing a surprising 2-0 victory in Sfax .
 The Mediterranean Knights enter the contest in second place in Group H with four points, while the Eagles of Carthage sit at the bottom of the standings with two points and are still searching for their first victory.
 The match will take place in Tripoli behind closed doors due to a CAF disciplinary sanction against the hosts.
 Kickoff is scheduled for 11:00 AM ET / 8:00 AM PT , with coverage beginning at 10:50 AM ET on beIN SPORTS CONNECT in the United States.
 Libya Looks to Build on Historic Victory and Strengthen Qualification Hopes
 Libya , managed by Senegalese coach Youssef Dabo , enters Tuesday's encounter with renewed confidence after recording its first victory in the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations Qualifiers .
 The Mediterranean Knights opened their campaign with a dramatic 2-2 draw against Botswana , recovering from a two-goal deficit through goals from Maruwan Alhibeeshi and Ezoo El Mariamy .
 However, their second match ended in a disappointing 1-0 away defeat against Uganda , putting additional pressure on the team ahead of its crucial double-header against Tunisia .
 Dabo's side responded emphatically on Friday, November 13, securing a 2-0 victory against the Eagles of Carthage at Stade Taïeb Mhiri in Sfax .
 Ali Youssif opened the scoring from the penalty spot in the 44th minute, before Hamdou El Houni doubled the advantage in the 62nd minute following an assist from Sayfulnasr Judour .
 That victory lifted Libya to four points, moving it into second place in Group H, just one point behind Uganda .
 The team has also received a timely boost ahead of the return fixture, with experienced winger Mohamed Tabbal returning to training in Tripoli after missing the first meeting.
 However, Libya will be unable to count on its supporters, as the match will be played behind closed doors following a disciplinary sanction imposed by CAF over incidents during a 2024 qualifier against Benin .
 Despite that setback, the Mediterranean Knights will be determined to repeat their recent success and take another important step toward qualification.
 Tunisia Faces Mounting Pressure After Another Disappointing Result
 Tunisia is experiencing a difficult qualifying campaign under head coach Moïne Chaâbani , having failed to win any of its opening three matches.
 The Eagles of Carthage began with a 1-1 home draw against Uganda on September 24. Adem Arous gave the hosts an early lead, but Rogers Mato equalized in the second half.
 Four days later, Tunisia was held to another draw, this time a 2-2 result against Botswana , despite two goals from striker Hazem Mastouri .
 The team's problems continued on November 13, when Libya produced a disciplined performance to secure a 2-0 victory in Sfax .
 Although Tunisia controlled much of the possession and recorded 13 shots, only two attempts were on target, highlighting the team's difficulty converting opportunities.
 The absence of Hazem Mastouri , who was ruled out of the November double-header through injury, has further complicated Chaâbani's attacking options.
 The coach will be hoping for a stronger contribution from experienced players such as Aïssa Laïdouni , Mohamed Ali Ben Romdhane , Ismaël Gharbi , and Montassar Talbi .
 With two points from three matches, the Eagles of Carthage face increasing pressure to secure a victory and avoid falling further behind their direct qualification rivals.
 A second consecutive defeat against Libya would leave the team in a particularly difficult position with only two matches remaining.
 A North African Rivalry With Major Group H Implications
 Tuesday's meeting between Libya and Tunisia carries significant consequences for the qualification race in Group H.
 After three rounds, Uganda leads with five points, followed by Libya with four, Botswana with three, and Tunisia with two.
 The qualification format adds another layer of importance to the encounter.
 As one of the three co-hosts of the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations , alongside Kenya and Tanzania , Uganda has already secured its place at the tournament.
 As a result, only the highest-ranked team among Libya , Botswana , and Tunisia will claim the group's remaining qualification spot.
 A second consecutive victory would take the Mediterranean Knights to seven points and establish a five-point advantage over their North African rivals with two matches remaining.
 Historically, Tunisia has enjoyed the upper hand in this fixture, winning both encounters during the 2023 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying campaign, including a 3-0 home victory and a 1-0 away win.
 However, Libya's recent triumph has shifted the momentum and given Dabo's team renewed belief that it can compete for a place at the continental finals.
 For Tunisia , which has appeared at 17 consecutive Africa Cup of Nations tournaments, another defeat would seriously threaten its hopes of extending that impressive run.
 With contrasting fortunes, a fierce regional rivalry, and valuable qualification points at stake, Tuesday's encounter promises to be one of the most significant matches of the international window.
